# Unequal midpoint coupling: sharp density capacity and a power tradeoff

These are local statements for two endpoints and an integer midpoint.
They do not give an iterated parity reduction or a depth comparison for
the geometric operation in Section 4.

Let d>=1 and let A,C be compact d-dimensional convex bodies with volumes
a,c>0. Write

    B_d(a,c)=((a^(1/d)+c^(1/d))/2)^d.                    (1)

The original endpoint volumes may differ. The two marginals of any
finite coupling necessarily have the SAME mass t; unpaired endpoint
mass must be left as a residual measure.

## 1. Sharp universal bound for a midpoint density

For every 0<t<=min(a,c), there are submeasures sigma_A<=1_A dx and
sigma_C<=1_C dx, each of mass t, and a coupling pi_t with those
marginals such that its midpoint pushforward eta satisfies

    eta <= [t/B_d(a,c)] dx.                              (2)

One can require the specific uniform fractional marginals

    sigma_A=(t/a)1_A dx, sigma_C=(t/c)1_C dx.             (3)

No smaller coefficient depending only on a,c,d,t works for all convex
A,C. For d=1 the coefficient in (2) is the exact optimal L-infinity
norm for every pair of intervals, regardless of their locations.

### Proof

Use the smooth triangular transport construction in Section 1 of
`candidate 71bcdfc8eb8340c6`. Its exact
properties needed here are the following. For the Gaussian-smoothed
uniform probability densities f<=1/a and g<=1/c, it constructs a
smooth triangular diffeomorphism T with positive diagonal derivatives
s_1,...,s_d, with T#(f dx)=g dx and

    product_i s_i=det DT=f/(g composed with T).

The map F=(Id+T)/2 is again a global triangular diffeomorphism. We
refine its determinant estimate, rather than replacing the triangular
map by an unproved optimal transport map. For positive s_i,

    product_i(1+s_i)
       >=[1+(product_i s_i)^(1/d)]^d.                  (4)

Indeed, the k-th elementary symmetric sum of the s_i is at least
binom(d,k)(product_i s_i)^(k/d), by applying arithmetic-geometric
mean to all k-element products. Summing those inequalities for
k=0,...,d proves (4).

The midpoint probability density at F(x) is therefore at most

    f(x)/det DF(x)
      <= [2/(f(x)^(-1/d)+g(T(x))^(-1/d))]^d
      <= 1/B_d(a,c).                                   (5)

The joint laws (X,T(X)) form a tight family as the smoothing scale
decreases to zero, because their two marginal laws converge to compactly
supported uniform laws. Extract a weak limit pi. It retains those exact
uniform marginals. Its midpoint pushforward is supported in (A+C)/2.
For every nonnegative compactly supported continuous test function,
pass (5) to the limit to obtain domination by dx/B_d(a,c). Multiplying
pi by t gives (2)-(3). This proof uses only the triangular construction
and its already proved Gaussian limiting argument.

For sharpness take A and C to be positive homothetic copies of a common
convex body. Their midpoint sum has volume exactly B_d(a,c). Every
possible midpoint measure of mass t is supported there, so its density
has essential supremum at least t/B_d(a,c) (and an unbounded density
does not improve that lower bound). The homothety coupling with
marginals (3) gives precisely uniform density t/B_d(a,c) on that sum.
This proves both the universal sharpness and the interval assertion.

## 2. Exact universal capacity for a mass-preserving paired output

If one removes endpoint submeasures of mass t each, preserving their
combined mass requires the midpoint output to be 2eta. The bound (2)
ensures that this output is dominated by Lebesgue measure provided

    t<=min(a,c,B_d(a,c)/2).                              (6)

This is the sharp maximum guaranteed uniformly from the three numbers
a,c,d. Marginal capacity forces t<=a,c; homothetic endpoints force
2t<=B_d(a,c), and their homothety coupling attains every t satisfying
(6). For intervals, (6) is the exact answer for the actual bodies:

    t_max=min(a,c,(a+c)/4).                              (7)

In particular, assuming a>=c, the whole smaller endpoint can be paired
while keeping the mass-preserving output density at most one precisely
under the following sharp volume-only sufficient condition:

    a/c >= (2*2^(1/d)-1)^d.                              (8)

For homothetic endpoints this condition is necessary as well. Equation
(8) is only about the output density; it does not provide unused room
inside an already occupied middle fiber.

For example, interval endpoints with lengths a=9,c=1 have midpoint-sum
length five. Pairing all of the smaller interval gives midpoint measure
eta of mass one and constant density 1/5; the mass-preserving output
2eta has density 2/5. For equal endpoint volumes a=c, by contrast,
mass-preserving domination permits only t<=a/2 in the homothetic case.

## 3. Cap cost and collision with the existing middle fiber

Put A,C at integer indices -1,+1. For every closed ambient halfspace H,
the affine midpoint identity gives

    eta(H_0)<=sigma_A(H_-1)+sigma_C(H_1).                (9)

This controls oblique normals and all boundary mass. The mass-preserving
output 2eta instead has the upper bound twice the right side. That
factor two is exact for the vertical cap {z>=0}: all midpoint mass 2t
is in the cap, while just the right endpoint contributes source mass t.

If the middle fiber K is already present with density one, adding 2eta
to its full uniform measure violates domination wherever eta has positive
density. More generally, a finite measure nu<=mu with nu(S)=mu(S)
must equal mu, since the nonnegative measure mu-nu has total mass zero.
Thus no nontrivial total-mass-preserving compression of the complete
three-fiber measure can also remain dominated by that original measure.
The local capacity (6) is not a way around this collision.

There is nonetheless a dimension-sensitive improvement to the separate
parity-class construction. If only the endpoints are in the input class,
independent volume-weighted base sampling uses

    t=ac/(a+c)

from each endpoint for its off-diagonal pairs. The midpoint density is
at most

    2ac/[(a+c)B_d(a,c)].                                (10)

This is no greater than one because

    B_d(a,c)>=sqrt(ac)>=2ac/(a+c).

It is the sharp volume-only replacement for the geometric-mean density
bound in that construction. For homothetic endpoints, use the homothety
coupling and attain the density in (10). For d=1 its exact expression
is 4ac/(a+c)^2. A separately retained middle parity class still adds its
own density there, so the overlap issue remains.

## 4. A genuine three-fiber geometric operation and its sharp power range

Suppose the actual three fibers are A,K,C at -1,0,+1, all of positive
d-volume, and K contains (A+C)/2. Put b=|K|. Brunn-Minkowski gives

    b>=B_d(a,c).                                        (11)

For 0<t<min(a,c), shrink A and C homothetically about arbitrary points
in themselves to volumes a-t and c-t. Expand K homothetically about
any of its points to volume b+2t. Denote the resulting bodies A_t,K_t,C_t.
The contractions remain subsets of A,C and the expansion contains K.
Hence

    (A_t+C_t)/2 subset K subset K_t.

The convex hull of these three layers has exactly A_t,K_t,C_t as its
integer fibers. For the middle assertion, any point of its zero section
is a convex combination of K_t and equal-weight endpoint midpoints,
already contained in K_t. The endpoint assertions follow from their
extreme integer indices. This is consequently an actual compatible
three-fiber operation, with conserved total volume M=a+b+c.

Let Phi_p be the sum of p-th powers of the three fiber volumes. For
every

    1<p<=1+1/d,

the operation strictly increases Phi_p for every t>0:

    (a-t)^p+(b+2t)^p+(c-t)^p>a^p+b^p+c^p.              (12)

Indeed, writing q=p-1 in (0,1/d], the power-mean inequality and (11)
give 2b^q>=a^q+c^q. The derivative of the left side is

    p[2(b+2t)^q-(a-t)^q-(c-t)^q],                       (13)

which is nonnegative at zero and strictly positive for every t>0.
Integration proves (12). Thus the specific effective-volume quantity

    [Phi_(1+1/d)/M]^d

also strictly increases under this operation, with M exactly conserved.

The exponent range is sharp. If a!=c and b=B_d(a,c), then for every
p>1+1/d strict power-mean monotonicity reverses the inequality at t=0:
the derivative in (13) is negative. This situation is realized by
homothetic endpoint bodies and their exact Minkowski midpoint body.
For an entirely rational example use d=2, endpoint squares of side
lengths 1 and 3, and their midpoint square of side length 2. Then
(a,b,c)=(1,4,9), and for p=2 the exact power difference is

    Phi_2(t)-Phi_2(0)=-4t+6t^2,

which is negative for 0<t<2/3. Taking t=1/4 gives -5/8.

The operation's new middle body may contain points outside the original
body. Its masses are not the dominated midpoint output of Section 2.
No monotonicity of maximum halfspace depth, no transfer of its new
centers back into the original set, and no iteration with preserved
cap constants is asserted. The exact potential (12) is a local
geometric fact; these missing properties are separate issues.
